slides.big: Nobody is more stressed than a man who got passed over, and now has to train the guy who got his promotion.
slides.small: And he can't afford to walk out.

You did the work for years.
They picked someone else.
Now you smile, show him the ropes, and drive home sick to your stomach.

It's not just the title.
It's the message: "All that work didn't count."
And you can't leave, because the bills don't stop.

slides.big: It happens more than you think.
slides.small: In an April 2026 Harris Poll of 1,334 U.S. workers, about 1 in 3 said a toxic boss cost them money through missed promotions or rewards.

slides.big: The fix: make them say it out loud.
slides.small:
Ask your boss one question:
"What exactly would I need to show you to get the next one?"
Then send it back in an email: "Just confirming what we discussed."
Now it's on paper.

slides.big:
Hard work in silence gets you passed over.
Hard work on paper gets you a case.

slides.big: If you've eaten lunch at your desk or in your truck more than 3 times this week, this is for you.
slides.small: You're not dedicated. You're running on fumes.

You "don't have time" for a break.
You eat with one hand and work with the other.
By 3 PM you're wiped out and short with everyone.

You skip the break so you look like a hard worker.
So nobody thinks you're slacking.
So you stay safe in a job you can't afford to lose.

slides.big: It's costing you more than lunch.
slides.small: In a Software Finder survey of 1,004 workers, nearly 2 in 5 said they end the day more exhausted after skipping a real lunch break.

slides.big: The fix: 15 minutes that are yours.
slides.small:
Walk away from the work spot.
Go outside if you can.
No work messages. Just eat and breathe.
Same time every day.

slides.big:
A break isn't laziness.
It's how you last.
